newsitem.title: USA: White House -- divided French government can work.
newsitem.headline: White House -- divided French government can work.

text.p: The election of a Socialist government in France will have no effect on strong Franco-American relations, the White House said on Monday.

"We have a very close working relationship with the French government. We continue to effectively explore our bilateral concerns during periods of cohabitation, and we look forward to working with the new government of Prime Minister Jospin," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.

The French election left U.S. President Bill Clinton and French President Jacques Chirac in a similiar position, having to work in tandem with their political oppposition. McCurry was diplomatic when asked if Clinton, who has faced Republican control of Congress since 1994, had any advice for Chirac.

"Well, the French political culture is much different than the political climate in the United States, but we ourselves have something of cohabitation. We know it can work," the White House spokesman said.
When asked about how the election would effect the push for a common currency in Europe as part of the European Economic and Monetary Union, or EMU, McCurry replied with a wisecrack.
"The EMU, for the benefit of those of you who don't know, is not a small furry creature that's on the endangered list," he quipped, referring to the flightless bird called an emu.

McCurry went on to note Treasury Secretrary Robert Rubin had recently said an integrated currency in Europe was good for global currency markets, and added that Rubin was "the authoritative spokesman on the issue."
